newsitem.title: SPAIN: NATO-Russia deal will not limit weapons - Germany.
newsitem.headline: NATO-Russia deal will not limit weapons - Germany.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruhe suggested on Thursday NATO would not be prevented from deploying modern weapons in new member states in Eastern Europe under an anticipated partnership accord with Russia.

Ruhe was speaking to reporters in Madrid where the 16-nation defence alliance is due to hold an expansion summit in July and invite at least three of Moscow's former Warsaw Pact allies -- Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to open negotiations on NATO membership.
NATO hopes to reach a partnership accord with Russia, which strongly opposes the expansion, before the summit.
Asked if the accord would prevent the alliance from deploying modern weapons in the new member states, Ruhe said: "No, that would be an erroneous interpretation."

Russia has conceded it cannot stop the expansion but has sought to win an agreement that NATO will not permanently station troops or build fresh bases on the territory of new member states. The United States has said it will not accept any deal that gives new member states second-class status.

Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov announced after talks in France on Wednesday that President Boris Yeltsin had accepted an invitation to go to Paris next month to sign the partnership accord.
